llms.body:
# AFR.IM — AI-Friendliness Rating

> AFR.IM publishes objective AI-friendliness ratings for websites: an open, reproducible 0–100 AFR score and an A–F grade showing how open each site is to AI crawlers and agents. Every point traces back to public evidence anyone can fetch again — robots.txt policy, llms.txt, sitemap, structured data, semantic HTML, public APIs, and agent instructions. English at https://afr.im/ and Chinese at https://afr.im/zh-CN/.

## Pages

- [Home](https://afr.im/): directory homepage — grade distribution, latest scans, and the natural leaderboard sorted by pure AFR score.
- [Method](https://afr.im/method): the full AFR standard — three layers, every sub-check and its points, grade thresholds, and the neutrality pledge.
- [Categories](https://afr.im/categories): browse rated sites by category.
- [Submit](https://afr.im/submit): request a scan of a site you care about.
- [About](https://afr.im/about): who runs AFR.IM and how to get in touch.
- [For bots](https://afr.im/bot): what our own scanner fetches and how a score is produced.
- [Badge](https://afr.im/badge): embeddable rating badge for your site.
- [Search](https://afr.im/search): search the directory.
- [Offline fallback](https://afr.im/offline): cached directory view shown when the network is unavailable.

## API — human-readable documentation

- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): every public endpoint, parameters, error shapes, and example JSON responses.
- [Machine-readable AFR standard](https://afr.im/api/v1/method): layers, per-check points, and grade thresholds as JSON.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://afr.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API (mirror at /.well-known/openapi.yaml).

## API endpoints

- [GET /api/v1/sites](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites): paginated directory listing with category, grade, search, and sort filters.
- [GET /api/v1/stats](https://afr.im/api/v1/stats): totals, grade distribution, and average score.
- [GET /api/v1/categories](https://afr.im/api/v1/categories): category tree with per-category site counts.
- [GET /api/v1/leaderboard](https://afr.im/api/v1/leaderboard): top sites by AFR score descending (never mixes in sponsored placements).
- [GET /badge/:domain.svg](https://afr.im/badge/example.com.svg): rating badge image for a domain.

## Optional: agent usage policy

- [Agent instructions](https://afr.im/agents.md): how to identify yourself, fetch budget, what content may be reused, and how to cite a rating.
- [AI crawler policy](https://afr.im/ai.txt): short machine-readable summary of what AFR.IM allows and why.
- [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt): explicit Allow rules for the 14 AI user-agent families plus the Sitemap declaration.
- Ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. See [About](https://afr.im/about) for contact and correction channels.

llmsFull.body:
# AFR.IM — AI-Friendliness Rating (full)

> AFR.IM publishes objective AI-friendliness ratings for websites: an open, reproducible 0–100 AFR score and an A–F grade showing how open each site is to AI crawlers and agents. This file is the complete variant of [llms.txt](https://afr.im/llms.txt): it lists every published page in both languages, the public API with example responses, and the agent usage policy. Every score is computed from public, reproducible evidence — see the [Method](https://afr.im/method) page for the standard.

## Core pages (English)

- [Home](https://afr.im/): grade distribution, latest scans, natural leaderboard, and category tiles.
- [Method](https://afr.im/method): the AFR standard in full — three layers (Reachability 35, Legibility 40, Actionability 25), every sub-check with its points, grade thresholds, engine versions, recompute guide, neutrality pledge, and data sources.
- [Categories](https://afr.im/categories): all 14 categories with site counts.
- [Search](https://afr.im/search): keyword search across the directory.
- [Submit](https://afr.im/submit): request a scan of a site.
- [About](https://afr.im/about): who runs the directory, corrections, and contact.
- [For bots](https://afr.im/bot): the endpoints our own scanner fetches and how points are awarded.
- [Badge](https://afr.im/badge): how to embed the rating badge on your site.
- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): public API reference with parameters and example JSON responses.
- [Offline fallback](https://afr.im/offline): cached directory view shown when the network is unavailable.

## Core pages (Chinese / zh-CN)

- [中文首页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/): 等级分布、最新扫描与自然排行榜。
- [评级方法](https://afr.im/zh-CN/method): AFR 标准全文——三层模型、全部子项与分值、等级阈值、复算指南与中立性承诺。
- [分类](https://afr.im/zh-CN/categories): 全部 14 个分类及站点数量。
- [搜索](https://afr.im/zh-CN/search): 目录关键词搜索。
- [提交站点](https://afr.im/zh-CN/submit): 申请扫描一个网站。
- [关于](https://afr.im/zh-CN/about): 运营方、纠错通道与联系方式。
- [机器人专用页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/bot): 我们的扫描器抓取哪些端点、分值如何产生。
- [徽章](https://afr.im/zh-CN/badge): 在你的网站上嵌入评级徽章。
- [API 文档](https://afr.im/zh-CN/docs): 公开 API 参考、参数与示例 JSON 响应。
- [离线回退页](https://afr.im/zh-CN/offline): 断网时显示的缓存目录视图。

## Categories (14, English)

- [Developer Tools](https://afr.im/c/dev-tools): SDKs, CLIs, and platforms for builders.
- [AI Applications & Assistants](https://afr.im/c/ai-tools): assistants, agents, and generative apps.
- [News & Media](https://afr.im/c/news): reporting and headlines from around the world.
- [E-commerce](https://afr.im/c/ecommerce): online stores and marketplaces.
- [Education](https://afr.im/c/education): courses, schools, and learning resources.
- [Finance](https://afr.im/c/finance): banking, markets, and financial data.
- [Social](https://afr.im/c/social): networks, communities, and messaging.
- [Entertainment](https://afr.im/c/entertainment): streaming, games, and culture.
- [Health](https://afr.im/c/health): health information and services.
- [Travel](https://afr.im/c/travel): booking, guides, and transport.
- [Government](https://afr.im/c/government): public sector and civic services.
- [Reference](https://afr.im/c/reference): encyclopedias, docs, and knowledge bases.
- [Developer documentation](https://afr.im/c/docs): documentation portals and API references.
- [Other](https://afr.im/c/other): everything outside the named categories.

Category pages also exist under the /zh-CN/ prefix, e.g. [中文 · Developer Tools](https://afr.im/zh-CN/c/dev-tools).

## Rated sites (sample directory entries)

- [github.com](https://afr.im/site/github.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [wikipedia.org](https://afr.im/site/wikipedia.org): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [stackoverflow.com](https://afr.im/site/stackoverflow.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [reuters.com](https://afr.im/site/reuters.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [openai.com](https://afr.im/site/openai.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [nytimes.com](https://afr.im/site/nytimes.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [linkedin.com](https://afr.im/site/linkedin.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.
- [example.com](https://afr.im/site/example.com): rated profile with full evidence chain and score history.

The same site pages exist under the /zh-CN/ prefix, e.g. [中文 · github.com](https://afr.im/zh-CN/site/github.com).

## API — human-readable documentation

- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): every public endpoint, parameters, error shapes, and example JSON responses.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://afr.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API (mirror at /.well-known/openapi.yaml).
- [Machine-readable AFR standard](https://afr.im/api/v1/method): `{ "standard": "AFR", "version": "...", "layers": [...], "grades": [...] }`.

## API endpoints

- [GET /api/v1/sites](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites): paginated listing; query params `category`, `grade`, `q`, `sort` (`score` | `rank` | `new`), `page`. Response: `{ "items": [...], "page": 1, "per_page": 24, "total": 8, "sort": "score" }`.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com): one site with its latest scan and evidence rows. Response: `{ "site": {...}, "scan": {...}, "evidence": [...] }`.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain/history](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com/history): all scans for a domain, newest first.
- [GET /api/v1/stats](https://afr.im/api/v1/stats): totals and distribution. Response: `{ "total": 8, "verified": 4, "pending": 0, "avg_score": 58, "grades": { "A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 2, "D": 2, "F": 1 } }`.
- [GET /api/v1/categories](https://afr.im/api/v1/categories): category tree with counts. Response: `{ "categories": [ { "slug": "dev-tools", "name_en": "Developer Tools", "name_zh": "开发者工具", "count": 3, "children": [] } ] }`.
- [GET /api/v1/leaderboard](https://afr.im/api/v1/leaderboard): top sites by pure AFR score descending; optional `category` and `limit` (≤50). Response: `{ "category": null, "items": [ { "rank": 1, "domain": "github.com", "grade": "A", "score": 91, "category": "dev-tools", "strategy_tag": "AI-Open" } ] }`.
- [GET /badge/:domain.svg](https://afr.im/badge/example.com.svg): rating badge image (`image/svg+xml`, cached 1 hour).
- [POST /api/v1/submissions](https://afr.im/api/v1/submissions): `{ "domain": "example.com", "note": "optional" }` → `201 { "ok": true, "id": 1, "domain": "example.com", "status": "queued" }`; limited to 5 per IP per day.

All JSON endpoints send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Errors are JSON, e.g. `{ "error": "not_found" }` (404) or `{ "error": "rate_limited" }` (429).

## Optional: agent usage policy

- [Agent instructions](https://afr.im/agents.md): identify yourself with a descriptive User-Agent, keep to about one request per second, honor robots.txt and any Crawl-delay, cache responses, and re-fetch only what changed.
- [AI crawler policy](https://afr.im/ai.txt): short machine-readable summary of what AFR.IM allows.
- [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt): explicit Allow rules for the 14 AI user-agent families (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended) plus the Sitemap declaration.
- Reuse: ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM and the site page URL; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. To cite a rating, include the domain, score, grade, engine version, and scan timestamp, and link back to the site's page on AFR.IM.

data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Method →</a> </div> <div class="ex-grid" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <article class="ex-card" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <h3 data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>What the score measures</h3> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Every rating on AFR.IM comes from one automated scan of a site's public signals — nothing behind a login, nothing that requires the site's cooperation. Each sub-check is a single HTTP request or DNS lookup that anyone can repeat from the command line.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>The 100 points split across three layers. Reachability (35) asks whether an AI crawler can reach the content at all: an explicit robots.txt policy for fourteen well-known AI user-agents, no challenge wall, and a homepage that answers. Legibility (40) asks whether a machine can understand what it fetched: llms.txt, structured data, semantic HTML, a sitemap, and basic content signals. Actionability (25) asks whether an agent can do real work with the site: call a published API, read agent instructions, or use documented machine interfaces.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Every awarded point carries its raw evidence — the URL that was fetched, the status code, and the rule that matched — so any score can be checked and recomputed. Grades are coordinates on an openness scale: A means openly available to AI systems, F means actively closed off.</p> </article> <article class="ex-card" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <h3 data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>What makes a site AI-friendly</h3> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>The strongest signal is a robots.txt that explicitly allows the AI crawlers you know about instead of silently defaulting or blocking them. After that come the basics of machine readability: pages that render as real HTML without JavaScript, headings that describe structure, images with alt text, a sitemap with lastmod dates, and an llms.txt file that maps your content for language models.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Sites that want to be useful to agents go one step further: a public HTTP API with a machine-readable OpenAPI specification, human-readable documentation, and an agents.md file that tells automated visitors who they are talking to, what they may fetch, and how to cite what they find. Stable HTTPS availability rounds it out — none of it matters if the homepage cannot be reached.</p> <p data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Ratings never depend on payment or popularity. Sponsored placements live only in separately labeled blocks and cannot change a grade or the natural ranking; verification, badges, and evidence chains stay free.</p> </article> </div> <p class="ex-links" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> <span class="ex-label mono" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Explore:</span> <a href="/method" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Method</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/docs" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>API documentation</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/llms.txt" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>llms.txt</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/agents.md" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>agents.md</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/openapi.json" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>OpenAPI</a> <span aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>·</span> <a href="/about" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>About</a> </p> <p class="ex-updated mono" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu> Directory data last updated <time datetime="2026-11-12T09:46:10.240Z" data-astro-cid-3he2njnu>Nov 12, 2026, 9:46 AM</time> </p> </section>  <script>

agentsMd.body:
# Agent instructions — AFR.IM

AFR.IM is a public directory of AI-friendliness ratings (AFR). This file tells automated visitors how to crawl it politely, what they may reuse, and how to cite a rating correctly. Humans are welcome too — start at [AFR.IM/about](https://afr.im/about).

## 1. Identify yourself

- Send a descriptive `User-Agent` that names your product and includes a contact URL or email, e.g. `MyCrawler/1.0 (+https://example.com/bot)`.
- If your operator publishes a verification page, link it from your UA. We do not block identified AI crawlers: all 14 known AI user-agent families are explicitly allowed in [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt), and the same open policy applies to everyone else.
- If you are acting on a user's behalf (fetch-on-demand), use your product's user-triggered UA rather than a generic bot UA.

## 2. Fetch budget and politeness

- Honor `robots.txt`, including any `Crawl-delay`, before every request.
- Keep to about **1 request per second** on HTML pages; the directory is small (tens of pages) and does not change between scans.
- Use conditional requests (`If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since`) where possible and cache responses; re-fetch only pages you detected as changed instead of polling.
- Do not retry aggressively: one retry after a 5xx or timeout, then back off. 4xx responses are final.
- `GET /badge/<domain>.svg` is cached for one hour upstream — reuse your copy inside that window.
- API endpoints are rate-limited (`POST /api/v1/submissions`: 5 per IP per day). GET endpoints need no key and send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

## 3. What you may reuse

- **Ratings, grades, check names, and score history:** reusable in your own answers and products with attribution to AFR.IM and a link to the site's page (see §4).
- **The AFR standard text** (the [Method](https://afr.im/method) page and the JSON at `/api/v1/method`): published under **CC BY 4.0** — reuse with attribution.
- **Page copy:** short factual quotes with attribution are fine; full-page republication is not.
- **Do not** present a rating without its context (score, grade, scan date, engine version), and **do not** imply endorsement by AFR.IM or by the rated site.

## 4. How to cite a rating

A complete citation has five parts: **domain, score, grade, engine version, scan timestamp**, plus a link back to the site's page on AFR.IM.

```text
github.com — 91/100 (grade A, AI-Open), AFR engine afr-1.1.0,
scanned 2026-11-10T11:40:00Z — https://afr.im/site/github.com
```

- The engine version lives on every result (`engineVersion`); recompute any score with it — see [Recompute](https://afr.im/method#recompute).
- The scan timestamp is the `scannedAt` field; always state it, because scores are snapshots.
- Link the standard when you explain what the number means: https://afr.im/method

## 5. Interfaces for agents

| Interface | URL | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| llms.txt (summary) | `/llms.txt` | map of the directory |
| llms-full.txt | `/llms-full.txt` | complete page inventory + API |
| robots.txt | `/robots.txt` | crawler policy (all AI families allowed) |
| sitemap.xml | `/sitemap.xml` | page inventory with lastmod |
| AI crawler policy | `/ai.txt` | short policy summary |
| Agent instructions | `/agents.md` | this file |
| Human API docs | `/docs` | endpoints, parameters, examples |
| OpenAPI spec | `/openapi.json` (mirror `/.well-known/openapi.yaml`) | machine-readable API |
| Machine-readable standard | `/api/v1/method` | layers, points, grade thresholds |
| For bots (our scanner) | `/bot` | what our own crawler fetches, how points are awarded |

## 6. Contact

Questions, corrections, or false-positive blocks: see [AFR.IM/about](https://afr.im/about), or open an issue in [github.com/AFR-IM/AFR-web](https://github.com/AFR-IM/AFR-web).
